audit_findings.title: The full cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $1,028.936 million, equal to $8.56/share and 9.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash to equity value; operating or seasonal cash should remain inside the operating business.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2026, we plan to use our cash resources to fund inventory purchases and inventory-related costs, employment-related costs, advertising costs, rental payments on our leases, stock repurchases and dividend payments, the payment of income taxes and property and equipment purchases.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification issue, not a demonstrated error. The filing expressly says cash funds inventory, payroll, rent, taxes and capital expenditures. Because the entire add-back represents nearly 10% of base equity value, the excess-cash determination can materially change the reported intrinsic value and buy-below threshold, although removing all cash would not reverse the current no-buy conclusion at $227.42.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating and seasonal cash from quarterly or monthly balances and working-capital needs, then rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Customer-funded float may be embedded in the cash add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: $618.926 million deferred-revenue face value; economic fulfillment claim unquantified; face value equals $5.15/share and 5.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer prepayments may support the cash balance while creating future fulfillment costs; value could be double counted through both the cash bridge and projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 1, 2026 and February 2, 2025, we had recorded $ 602.9 million and $ 584.8 million, respectively, for gift card and other deferred revenue within current liabilities in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The customer-funded liability is demonstrated, but neither the associated cash nor its economic fulfillment cost is established. Deducting the full liability would be inappropriate because future recognized revenue offsets merchandise and service costs. Its face value is large enough to warrant investigation, but the record cannot determine the net value effect or establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile deferred-revenue cash receipts, redemptions, breakage, fulfillment costs and owner-earnings working-capital adjustments; rerun only for the quantified net economic obligation already represented in bridge cash.

audit_findings.title: Committed but uncommenced leases are absent from the anchor period
audit_findings.magnitude: $205.9 million of undiscounted future payments, equal to $1.71/share if mechanically treated as a dollar-for-dollar claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent will reduce projected owner earnings, while the associated stores or facilities may add revenue and earnings; neither effect is present in the historical anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, we have future payment obligations of $ 205.9 million relating to executed lease agreements for which the related lease terms had not yet commenced as of February 1, 2026, and, therefore, are not included in the table above.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is filed, but it is forward-looking and its gross amount is not a present-value loss. Even an overly conservative dollar-for-dollar deduction would equal only 2.0% of base equity value and would not change the present valuation conclusion. The relevant future net operating burden remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Track commencement dates, annual rent, opening capital expenditure and incremental earnings; incorporate the net owner-earnings effect when the leases commence or when reliable projections become available.

audit_findings.title: The latest-quarter zero-debt and senior-claims assertion was not successfully parsed
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 borrowings at August 2, 2026; $13.6 million of undrawn standby letters of credit, equal to 1.3% of cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Actual borrowings could require a bridge or owner-earnings timing adjustment, but undrawn letters of credit and ordinary operating liabilities do not create funded debt.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, we had no borrowings under our Credit Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied 10-Q resolves the failed parse: it explicitly reports no borrowings during the quarter or first half, presents no funded debt on the August 2 balance sheet, and reports no amounts outstanding under separate letter-of-credit facilities. The $13.6 million of standby letters of credit was undrawn and secured already-recorded insurance liabilities. Thus the bridge's zero funded-debt input is supported.
audit_findings.action: No rerun is needed; retain the 10-Q balance sheet and borrowing-note citations in the valuation record.

audit_findings.title: Anchor earnings contain a potentially nonrecurring inventory-count benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $39.034 million pre-tax, $29.237 million after tax at 25.1%, or 4.4% of the $669.6 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecurring favorable inventory-count adjustment inflates anchor owner earnings and therefore projected owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This decrease in gross margin of 30 basis points was driven by (i) the out-of-period freight adjustment in the first quarter of fiscal 2024 of 70 basis points, (ii) lower merchandise margins of 40 basis points as a result of the flow-through of tariffs into cost of goods sold, and (iii) the deleverage of occupancy costs of 20 basis points, partially offset by (iv) supply chain efficiencies of 50 basis points, including lower shipping costs, reductions in damages and returns, reduced replacements, as well as fewer customer accommodations, and (v) favorable physical inventory results of 50 basis points.
audit_findings.explanation: The 50-basis-point benefit is demonstrated, but the filing does not establish that it was entirely nonrecurring. Even treating all of it as nonrecurring gives an after-tax ceiling of about $29.2 million. Proportionally reducing the base operating PV would lower base value by about $3.42/share, from $86.85 to approximately $83.43, which does not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $227.42 price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the physical-inventory and shrink-reserve roll-forward; if a discrete true-up is identified, rerun the anchor and scenarios after removing only its after-tax amount.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling mixes award inventory and common shares from different dates
audit_findings.magnitude: 2.396030 million dated award inventory and 0.617 million net first-half share releases; net mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted released awards overstate diluted shares and understate value per share, while omitted post-year grants would understate diluted shares and overstate value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Shares issued as a result of award exercises or releases are primarily funded with the issuance of new shares.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but its net direction is unresolved because releases, cancellations, new grants and PSU outcomes must be rolled forward together. The entire February award inventory is only 2.0% of the 120.175203 million denominator. Even removing all 2.396030 million awards would raise base value only from $86.85 to approximately $88.62 and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build an August 2, 2026 award roll-forward covering grants, releases, cancellations and probable PSU payouts, then rerun per-share values with the date-consistent dilution ceiling.
